Buccaneer Cove is best explored from the water. On Santiago Island's northwestern coast, cliffs rise above the ocean, their hollows and ledges carved by wind and waves. Isolated rock stacks stand nearby. As the boat gradually changes position, the same stretch of shoreline takes on a different appearance with every view.

The cove's name recalls the buccaneers who used anchorages like this while sailing across the Pacific. Ships could shelter here and undergo repairs. Today, the seabirds perched on the cliffs, the animals near the water and the shape of the volcanic coastline draw visitors' attention.

On a boat trip, you can compare the dry upper rocks with the lower strip continually worked by the surf. Bird traces mark the dark stone, shadows gather in the crevices, and the water changes colour around coastal outcrops. Buccaneer Cove appeals to photographers and lovers of maritime history. A visit often complements other stops on Santiago Island, although the form of the excursion depends on the particular cruise itinerary.

Buenos Aires is best explored neighbourhood by neighbourhood. La Boca and San Telmo, Plaza de Mayo and Casa Rosada, the Obelisk and Corrientes Avenue, museums, galleries and theatres can easily be spread across 2–3 days, depending on your interests.

You can set aside a separate day for Tigre: travel to the Paraná Delta and take a catamaran between its islands and waterways.

Another full-day option takes you into the Argentine Pampas and to an estancia, for an introduction to gaucho life, horse riding, local cuisine, music and equestrian performances. In the evening, you can add a tango show to your city itinerary.

Búzios grew from a small fishing village into a resort where the coastline itself is the main attraction. Here, it is easy to alternate beach time with boat trips, diving, surfing, kayaking and buggy rides between different parts of the peninsula.


Viewpoints offer panoramas of the ocean, coves and green hills. You can shape your time on the water as you wish: stops for swimming and snorkelling, a leisurely cruise along the coast or a more active day.


In the evening, activity shifts towards Rua das Pedras and the nearby streets. It is a lovely way to end a beach day and a good reason to spend more than one night in Búzios, especially when the resort is the next stop after Rio de Janeiro.
